texts.error.no_file: No game is in the project.
texts.error.no_gl_bridge: Vita3K draws with OpenGL on the GPU, and no GPU was handed over (the renderer setting is opengl-hw, and this machine may have no OpenGL context to give).
texts.error.no_log: The log could not be made.
texts.error.no_user: There is no user to give the save data to.

texts.error.not_a_game: %1 is not a game on its own: it installs %2 (category %3), which belongs to a game.
texts.error.not_font_package: %1 installed nothing in %2: it is not the font package (is it the system software, PSVUPDAT.PUP?).
texts.error.not_installed: %1 did not install: the package is damaged, or %2 is another game's licence.
texts.error.not_system_software: %1 installed nothing in %2: it is not the system software (is it the font package, PSP2UPDAT.PUP?).
texts.error.not_work_bin: %1 is not a licence: a work.bin is the 512 bytes the console keeps for the game.
texts.error.not_zrif: %1 is not a licence: a text licence is a zRIF, one line of letters and digits.
texts.error.package_needs_licence: %1 is a package, and a package is encrypted. Put the game's licence (its work.bin, or its zRIF in a .txt file) in the Licence slot.
texts.error.package_no_content: %1 names no content: it is not a package Vita3K can install.
texts.error.save_data_unreadable: The save data %1 cannot be read.

texts.error.size_fixed: The picture's size cannot change once the machine has drawn.
texts.error.vitamin: This file is a copy of the game made with the tool Vitamin, which Vita3K does not run. A copy made with NoNpDrm, or the game's .pkg with its licence, is what it takes.
texts.firmware.psp2updat_pup.about: The Vita's font package. Vita3K installs it before the game starts. Games that draw text with the system fonts need it.
texts.firmware.psvupdat_pup.about: The Vita's system software update, as PlayStation publishes it. Vita3K installs it before the game starts. The system libraries most games load come from it.
texts.setting.cpu_mhz.about: How fast the console's processor runs. The game's code uses up emulated time at this speed. The default, 1332, is the Vita's three 444 MHz processor cores added together, counted at one instruction per cycle. It is part of the machine.
texts.setting.enter_button.about: Which button confirms in the system's dialogs and in games that follow the system setting. It is Cross outside Japan and Circle on Japanese consoles. Games read it, so it is part of the machine.
texts.setting.internal_resolution.about: How many times the Vita's 960x544 resolution the graphics card draws at (Vita3K's Internal Resolution Upscaling). Above 1x the picture Chimera shows and records is the larger one, for example 1920x1088 at 2x. 3D shapes get finer edges. Text and images made for 960x544 are only enlarged. It is part of the machine. What the graphics card draws is written back into the Vita's memory at the Vita's own size, reduced from the larger picture, so those bytes differ from the ones a 1x picture leaves, and a game that reads its own picture can tell the difference. Measured on Alien Breed (1500 frames) and Alien Shooter (300 frames), the machine's timing, its thread switches and its sound are the same at 2x as at 1x. One limit: a savestate holds the picture at 960x544 and not the larger one, so in the first frame after a state is loaded the picture can be the small one enlarged. The machine itself is the same, and a movie played from the start is drawn at the chosen size throughout. Choose the resolution when the project is made, because an existing movie does not fit another resolution. Higher resolutions need more graphics power: 4x has sixteen times the pixels of 1x.
texts.setting.language.about: The console's system language. Games read it to choose their language, so it is part of the machine.
texts.setting.ngs.about: Vita3K's 'Enable NGS Support' option. NGS is the Vita's sound library for games that mix their own sound. With it on, the core runs the library and those games have their sound. With it off, every NGS call returns at once without doing anything, and a game that uses NGS is silent or misses some sounds. It is on unless you turn it off here. Turn it off only for a game that hangs or crashes inside NGS, because Vita3K's NGS is not complete. What a game gets back from the library affects its timing (a game may wait for a sound to end), so it is part of the machine and a movie made with it off needs it off.
texts.setting.renderer.about: How the picture is drawn. Both choices are Vita3K's own renderers and both draw on your computer's graphics card: "vulkan-hw" with Vulkan, "opengl-hw" with OpenGL. Vulkan is the default because it is Vita3K's own default. It needs a graphics driver that has Vulkan and a Chimera that hands Vulkan to cores (Development build 4ca6e302 or later); without either the project does not start and says why, and "opengl-hw" is the one to choose. Vita3K has no renderer that works without a graphics card, so this core cannot run on a computer that offers neither. The two do not draw every pixel alike, so a movie should be played back with the renderer it was made with if its pictures are to match. With either one, what the graphics card draws is also written back into the Vita's memory, so a savestate holds the pictures.
texts.setting.rendering_accuracy.about: Vita3K's 'High Accuracy' option, for the Vulkan renderer. With "standard", Vita3K's own default, the renderer takes two shortcuts that are faster and right in most games. With "high" it takes neither: a game that reads back what it has just drawn gets exactly that, and textures are sampled the exact way. Some games' pictures are only right with "high"; it is slower, and needs a graphics driver that has the 'fragment shader interlock' feature for the first of the two (without it only the second changes). The OpenGL renderer does not read this setting. The two values do not draw every pixel alike, so a movie should be played back with the one it was made with if its pictures are to match.
texts.setting.rtc_start.about: The date the console's clock shows when the game starts, in seconds since 1970. For example 1356998400 is 2013-01-01. After the start the clock runs with the emulated console and never with your computer. It is part of the machine. A game that picks its random numbers from the time plays differently with another date.
texts.setting.system_software.about: Which of the Vita's system files are installed in the machine. Most games need the system software (PSVUPDAT.PUP, from PlayStation's update page) for its system libraries, and the font package (PSP2UPDAT.PUP) for the system fonts. 'Full' installs both. 'Fonts' installs only the font package. 'None' is for homebrew built with the Vita SDK, which needs neither. They are installed before the game starts, so they are part of the machine.
texts.slot.game.help: The game, in one of three forms. It can be a .vpk file. It can be a NoNpDRM dump packed as a .zip (the game's folder, including its sce_sys/package/work.bin). Or it can be a PlayStation Store package (.pkg), with the game's licence in the Licence slot. Vita3K installs it into the machine before it starts. Vita3K's compatibility list (vita3k.org/compatibility) says which games work.
texts.slot.licence.help: The licence that decrypts a .pkg game. It is the game's work.bin (the 512-byte file a NoNpDRM dump keeps in sce_sys/package), the console's own .rif file for the game, or a .txt file holding the licence as a zRIF (one line of letters and digits, as NoPayStation lists it and a KEY.txt beside a package holds it). A package is encrypted and installs nothing without it. A .vpk or a .zip dump needs none, because a dump includes its own. The project and the movie record exactly which file was used, as they do for the game.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the game already saved, as Emulator > Export Save Data... wrote it. It is a .zip with savedata/<TITLE ID>/... (the system's save data) and data/... (where homebrew keeps its files). A save copied from a Vita with ux0:/user/00/ in front of the path, or a plain <TITLE ID>/ folder, is accepted too. It is put into the machine before the game starts.
